bibliographic.title: Technical, legal, and ethical challenges of generative artificial intelligence: an analysis of the governance of training data and copyrights
bibliographic.authors: Marcelo Pasetti; James William Santos; Nicholas Kluge Corrêa; Nythamar de Oliveira; Camila Palhares Barbosa
bibliographic.citation_apa: Pasetti, M., Santos, J. W., Corrêa, N. K., de Oliveira, N., & Barbosa, C. P. (2025). Technical, legal, and ethical challenges of generative artificial intelligence: an analysis of the governance of training data and copyrights. Discover Artificial Intelligence, 5, 193. https://doi.org/10.1007/s44163-025-00379-6

methodology.study_design: comparative regulatory and doctrinal analysis across jurisdictions
methodology.sample_description: Regulatory frameworks and legal doctrines in the United States, European Union, Japan, and Brazil
methodology.technology_context: Generative AI and LLMs discussed primarily in relation to training data, copyright-protected content, and model training; chatbots mentioned only as an example application of LLMs

eligibility.decision_rationale: The article centrally addresses governance of generative AI training data, copyright compliance, transparency, and audit mechanisms across legal jurisdictions. It mentions LLMs and online chatbots only peripherally and does not examine conversational systems, deployment-time guardrails, human oversight, contestability, or post-deployment monitoring. It is relevant as supporting evidence for broader GenAI governance themes but not as central evidence for conversational governance in regulated LLM systems.
eligibility.manual_spotcheck_reason: Extracted Python title metadata is corrupted; conversational relevance is weak despite high deterministic term scores and requires human confirmation of scope fit.

appraisal.notes: Appropriate for a comparative legal-philosophical article on copyright and training-data governance. Empirical sampling and data-collection procedures are not evidenced in the provided excerpts. Conversational-AI governance is not a stated objective.

cerqual.explanation: The study is internally coherent for copyright and training-data governance of generative AI, but its adequacy and relevance to conversational governance in deployed LLM systems are only partial because the focus is legal doctrine, dataset opacity, and compensation rather than conversational control, oversight, or operational governance.

coding.theme: Governance of generative AI training data and copyright
coding.subtheme: Comparative legal frameworks for transparency, compensation, and audit

synthesis.main_claim: Existing copyright and text-and-data-mining mechanisms in major jurisdictions are inadequate to address opacity and legal uncertainty in generative AI training datasets; governance should include mandatory transparency, ethical compensation for rights holders, and robust audit mechanisms.
synthesis.contribution: Provides a comparative legal-philosophical analysis of generative AI training-data governance across the United States, European Union, Japan, and Brazil, linking transparency deficits to legal accountability, epistemic risk, and distributive asymmetry.
synthesis.use_in_review: Use as supporting evidence for cross-cutting GenAI governance themes such as transparency, audit, compliance, and accountability in regulated legal contexts; do not treat as central evidence on conversational governance, human oversight, or operational controls in deployed LLM/chatbot systems.
